name: dayfile
description: Your journal as long-term memory: days drafted from git, calendar and photos, facts with a timeline, all in Markdown files you own.
long_description: Dayfile keeps entries and memory as plain Markdown files in a folder you own. This extension runs the bundled `dayfile` CLI as an MCP server over stdio with 19 tools and two prompts: search and edit entries, draft a day from your commits, calendar feeds and photos, and record and recall facts about your life with valid time and recorded time. It uses the folder the Dayfile desktop app is set to, or ~/Journal.

tools.name: list_entries
tools.description: List entries, newest first, with filters

tools.name: on_this_day
tools.description: Entries from this day in other years

tools.name: append_to_today
tools.description: Append a paragraph to today's entry

tools.name: update_entry
tools.description: Update body, tags, star or journal

tools.name: delete_entry
tools.description: Move an entry to the trash

tools.name: capture_day
tools.description: Draft a day from git, calendar and photos

tools.name: accept_draft
tools.description: Keep a draft as an entry

tools.name: remember
tools.description: Record a fact about the user's life

tools.name: recall
tools.description: Facts true on a date, as known at a moment

tools.name: fact_history
tools.description: Every fact of a topic over time

tools.name: retract_fact
tools.description: Mark a fact as never true

prompts.name: review_day
prompts.description: Turn a captured day into an entry and update memory

prompts.name: weekly_review
prompts.description: Look back over seven days and what changed in memory
